st: Put the dried attieke in a large bowl and sprinkle with [[1 cup]] hot water. Cover and let it soak for 10 minutes.
Fluff the grains with a fork, breaking up all lumps.
Line a steamer basket with a clean cloth and set it over simmering water.
Steam the attieke for 15 minutes until hot and light.
Tip it into a bowl and fluff again with a fork. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Mix the onion, tomatoes, chili and lime juice in another bowl with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Serve the attieke warm with the tomato salad and cucumber, alongside grilled fish or chicken.
Cut the plantains into chunks about 1 inch thick.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and toss.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the plantain chunks in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and caramelized.
Lift out and drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but [[1 tbsp]] oil. Cook the onion, tomato and chili for 3 minutes to make a quick sauce.
Serve the hot alloco with the onion and chili sauce spooned on top.
Soak the dried attieke with [[1 cup]] hot water for 10 minutes, then fluff and steam for 15 minutes until hot.
Season the tuna with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the tuna for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden outside and just cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and break into large chunks.
Mix the onion, tomatoes and chili in a bowl with a spoonful of the hot frying oil.
Heap the attieke onto plates and add the tuna and the onion mixture.
Serve at once with extra chili sauce if you like heat.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Put the chicken, onions, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, whole chili, eggplant, thyme and [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot with a tight lid.
Add [[0.5 tsp]] salt and mix well. Do not add any water, as the vegetables will release liquid.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 30 minutes.
Holding the lid on firmly, shake the pot every 10 minutes so nothing sticks. Keep cooking for another 45 minutes.
Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the sauce is thick.
Remove the thyme stems and whole chili.
Serve hot with attieke, rice or plantains.
Put the plantains, yam and cassava in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, then cook for 30 minutes until everything is very soft.
Drain, keeping about [[1 cup]] of the cooking water.
Mash in a bowl, or pound in a mortar, adding a splash of the water at a time.
Keep working for about 10 minutes until the dough is completely smooth, stretchy and sticky.
With wet hands, shape into 4 smooth balls.
Drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] palm oil if using, and serve warm with a palm nut or peanut sauce.
Soak the smoked fish in hot water for 15 minutes, then flake and remove bones.
Put the chicken, onion, tomatoes, whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large pot with [[1 cup]] water. Boil for 25 minutes.
Add the eggplant and cook 10 more minutes.
Remove the eggplant, mash it, and set aside.
Stir in the palm nut cream, [[2 cups]] water and the flaked fish. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and dark red and the oil rises.
Stir the mashed eggplant back in. Chicken must reach 165°F (74°C).
Remove the whole chili and adjust the salt. Serve with rice, foutou or attieke.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and whole chili and cook 6 minutes until soft.
Whisk [[0.75 cup]] peanut butter with [[1 cup]] hot water until smooth and stir it into the pot.
Return the chicken, add [[2 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 40 minutes, stirring from the bottom, until the sauce is thick and the chicken is 165°F (74°C).
Remove the whole chili. Serve with rice, foutou or attieke.
Soak the smoked fish in hot water for 15 minutes, then flake and remove bones.
Mix the cassava flour with [[1.5 cups]] cold water in a bowl until smooth and lump free.
Bring [[2 cups]] water to a boil in a heavy pot. Slowly stir in the cassava mixture.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until it is thick, smooth and glossy. Keep warm.
For the sauce, heat [[2 tbsp]] palm oil and cook the onion for 3 minutes. Add the okra, fish, whole chili, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the okra is soft and the sauce is slightly slimy.
Shape the placali into balls with wet hands.
Serve with the okra sauce spooned on top.

ing: such as tilapia or sea bream, cleaned and scored
st: Mix half the garlic with the ginger, [[1 tbsp]] oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Rub it inside and over the fish.
Marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat the grill or broiler to high.
Grill the fish for 8 minutes per side, until the skin is charred and the flesh is opaque and flakes at 145°F (63°C).
For the sauce, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the rest of the garlic, tomatoes, chili and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the mustard and lime juice and cook 1 minute.
Spoon the hot sauce over the fish and serve with attieke or fried plantains.
Put the ginger and [[1 cup]] of the water in a blender and blend until smooth.
Add the pineapple and blend again.
Strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth into a pitcher, pressing hard on the pulp.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] sugar until dissolved, then the lemon juice.
Add the remaining [[4 cups]] cold water and the mint leaves.
Taste. Add more sugar for sweetness or more water to make it milder.
Chill for at least 20 minutes.
Serve over [[2 cups]] ice.
